---
title: "Tidy Tuesday 2025-09-30: Cranes"
format: html
---


```{r}
#| label: setup

library(tidyverse)

cranes <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2025/2025-09-30/cranes.csv') |> 
    mutate(obs_year = factor(year(date)),
           numeric_year = year(date),
           day_of_year = yday(date)) |> 
    filter(!is.na(observations) & observations > 0) |> 
    arrange(date)
  
glimpse(cranes)

```


```{r}
#| label: point plot cranes

# Create a point chart with day of year on x-axis and separate lines per year
cranes |> 
  group_by(obs_year) |>
  mutate(
    date_diff = c(NA, diff(date)),
    new_group = cumsum(is.na(date_diff) | date_diff > 14) # Break if gap > 14 days
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = day_of_year, y = observations, color = obs_year)) +
#   geom_line(aes(group = paste(obs_year, new_group)), linewidth = 1.2, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5, alpha = 0.6) +
  labs(
    title = "Crane Observations Throughout the Year",
    x = "Day of Year",
    y = "Number of Cranes Observed",
    color = "Year"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 32, 60, 91, 121, 152, 182, 213, 244, 274, 305, 335),
                     labels = c("Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", 
                               "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec")) +
  theme_minimal()
```

What date has the maximum observerved cranes each year in the spring migration?
Does the date of the first observation change over the years? 

```{r}
#| label: median arrival spring and fall

x <- cranes |> 
  mutate(day_of_year = yday(date), 
         season = case_when(
           day_of_year <= 150 ~ "Spring",
           day_of_year >= 150 ~ "Fall",
           TRUE ~ "Other"
         )) |> 
  filter(season != "Other") |> 
  group_by(obs_year, season) |>
  summarise(max_observations = max(observations),
            max_day = day_of_year[which.max(observations)],
            num_observations = n(),
            total_cranes = sum(observations),
            .groups = "drop")


m <- x |> 
  group_by(season) |>
  summarise(median_day = median(max_day),
            .groups = "drop")
```


```{r}
#| label: plot median arrival spring and fall

spring <- x |> 
  filter(season == "Spring")

spring |> 
  arrange(obs_year) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = median_day, y = obs_year)) +
  # geom_path(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Median Arrival Days of Cranes in Spring and Fall",
    x = "Day of Year",
    y = "Number of Observations per Year",
    color = "Season"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() + 
  facet_wrap(~season)

```





```{r}
#| label: number of observations per year

obs <- cranes |> 
  filter(!is.na(observations) & observations > 0) |>
  group_by(obs_year) |>
  summarise(total_observations = n(),
            total_cranes = sum(observations),
            .groups = "drop")
```


I want to make a diverging bar chart of the first day of observations in spring every year. 

```{r}
# Calculate first observation day for each year in spring
spring_timing <- cranes |>
  mutate(day_of_year = yday(date)) |>
  filter(day_of_year <= 150) |>  # Spring observations only
  group_by(obs_year) |>
  summarise(
    first_observation = min(day_of_year),
    peak_day = day_of_year[which.max(observations)],
    total_spring_cranes = sum(observations),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(year_numeric = as.numeric(as.character(obs_year)))

# Check for trend in first observation timing
spring_timing |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year_numeric, y = first_observation)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "darkred") +
  labs(
    title = "First Spring Crane Observation Over Years",
    subtitle = "Is crane arrival getting earlier?",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Day of Year (First Observation)"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = c(60, 75, 90, 105, 120),
    labels = c("Mar 1", "Mar 16", "Mar 31", "Apr 15", "Apr 30")
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Statistical test for trend
cor.test(spring_timing$year_numeric, spring_timing$first_observation)
```



```{r}
# Check if peak timing is also shifting
spring_timing |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year_numeric, y = peak_day)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "lightgrey") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "darkred") +
  labs(
    title = glue::glue("Peak Spring Crane Observation 1994-2024"),
    subtitle = "Is the peak crane observation date shifting?",
    x = "Year", 
    y = "Day of Year (Peak Observation)"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = c(60, 75, 90, 105, 120),
    labels = c("Mar 1", "Mar 16", "Mar 31", "Apr 15", "Apr 30")
  ) +  
  theme_minimal()


cor.test(spring_timing$year_numeric, spring_timing$peak_day)
```
